summary:
The research points to one main rule. People prefer to touch the middle of the screen and are most accurate there: about 7 mm at the centre against about 12 mm at the corners and top and bottom edges. The comfortable thumb area does not grow with the phone (about 36 cm² measured on phones up to 6 inches), so on 6.1–6.9 inch phones it covers only about a third of the screen. Users also shift their grip often, so no area is truly unreachable, but the top 30–40% and the corner nearest the base of the thumb are slow and less accurate.

Recommendation: five native tabs, Home · Vaults · Pay · Invest · Emergency. Pay is a normal centre tab, not a raised button. Apple's guidelines say tab bars are for navigation, not actions. A raised button would also need a custom JavaScript tab bar instead of Expo's native tabs. The centre slot is the only bottom position that is easy to reach with either thumb. The current More tab becomes an avatar menu in the top corner for settings, with its other items moved into the relevant screens. Option B, which keeps More and moves Emergency off the tab bar, is the fallback. Everything that moves money opens as a full-screen modal. Each has one full-width primary button, 56pt tall, sitting 16pt above the home indicator, and keypads sit in the lower-middle of the screen.

The thumb-zone percentages are my own synthesis of studies on 4–6 inch phones. They should be checked with the in-app reach test described in the spec.

findings.claim: In Hoober's 2013 field observation of mobile users, about half of the people touching the screen held the phone in one hand, and one-handed use was mostly with the right thumb.
findings.evidence: 1,333 observations, 780 touching the screen: 49% one-handed, 36% cradled, 15% two-handed. Of the one-handed users, 67% used the right thumb and 33% the left. The largest phone seen was a Galaxy Note 2.

findings.claim: Hoober later withdrew his 2013 reach drawings. His 2017 work says about 75% of touches are made with one thumb, but fewer than half of users hold the phone one-handed, and grips change constantly without users noticing.
findings.evidence: A 2017 editor's note and comment on the 2013 article ask readers to disregard the drawings. Part 1 (2017) reports 36% cradling and 10% holding in one hand while tapping with the other hand's finger. It also says users reach the top Back button constantly by shifting their grip.

findings.claim: Touch is most accurate and most preferred at the centre of the screen. Accuracy is about 7 mm at the centre and about 12 mm at the corners. The top and bottom edges are worse than the sides.
findings.evidence: Hoober (Part 3, 2017) reports 7 mm at the centre and 12 mm at the corners, based on millions of measured touches. His 2013 article recommends 10–12 mm spacing at the top and bottom edges, at most four items in a bottom bar, and padding below lists so items can be scrolled into the middle. Part 2 adds that people scroll content toward the centre.

findings.claim: Hoober recommends putting key actions in the middle half to two-thirds of the screen and secondary actions and tabs along the top and bottom. Tertiary functions belong in menus opened from a corner. Unrecoverable actions should be kept away from routine controls.
findings.evidence: These are the explicit heuristics in Part 3 (July 2017). The same article advises at most four items on an iOS bar, or five on the largest phones.

findings.claim: Region-specific target sizes attributed to Hoober's book (top 11 mm, bottom 12 mm, centre 7 mm) are published with unit conversions that are wrong for iPhones.
findings.evidence: Smart Interface Design Patterns (2023) converts 11 mm to 31 pt, which uses typographic points (1/72 inch). On current 460 ppi @3x iPhones, 1 pt is about 0.166 mm, so 11 mm is about 66 pt and 12 mm about 72 pt. This conversion is my own calculation.

findings.claim: The thumb's comfortable area (reachable without losing grip stability) is roughly constant at about 36 cm², whatever the phone size. On larger phones the grip moves toward the top.
findings.evidence: Le, Mayer, Bader & Henze (CHI 2018) tested 16 participants with hand sizes from 163 to 219 mm on 4–5.96 inch phones. Thumb comfortable area was 33.6–41.9 cm² (mean 36.4) with no significant link to phone size. Inference: that is about 39% of a 6.1 inch screen and about 33% of a 6.7 inch screen.

findings.claim: Bergstrom-Lehtovirta and Oulasvirta model the thumb's functional area as a quadratic arc. Its size depends on hand size, screen size and where the index finger sits on the back of the phone.
findings.evidence: The CHI 2014 abstract describes a quadratic model fitted to 20 participants that can be used both to check layouts and to infer grips. Le et al. 2018 summarise its average R² as 0.958. I could not access the full text, which is paywalled.

findings.claim: The corner nearest the base of the thumb (bottom-right for right-handed use) gives the worst one-handed tapping performance. Smaller phones and side-to-side thumb movements perform best.
findings.evidence: Trudeau et al. (J Biomech 2012, 10 participants) found the poorest performance near the thumb base in the bottom-right, where the thumb is strongly bent, and the best in neutral postures (top-right and middle-left on the phones tested). Trudeau et al. (Human Factors 2012, 20 participants) found better performance on smaller phones, side-to-side movement better than bending movement, and outward movement better than inward.

findings.claim: Hurff's Thumb Zone is a best-guess heat map, credited to Luke Wroblewski, not a measured result. Its useful point is that the natural zone stays about the same size while the hard-to-reach area grows on bigger phones.
findings.evidence: The September 2014 article describes a right-thumb map anchored at the bottom-right. It says the safe zone does not scale with the screen and that the 6 Plus has more hard-to-reach area.

findings.claim: For one-handed thumb use, targets of 9.2 mm suit single taps and 9.6 mm suit repeated tapping such as keypads.
findings.evidence: Parhi, Karlson & Bederson, MobileHCI 2006. NN/g (2019) cites this study for its 1 cm × 1 cm minimum. On current iPhones 9.6 mm is about 58 pt.

findings.claim: Standard Fitts's law under-predicts touch errors on small targets, because finger touch has a fixed precision limit in addition to the usual speed-accuracy trade-off.
findings.evidence: Bi, Li & Zhai, CHI 2013. Their FFitts model explains significantly more variance (R² of 0.91 or higher) in 1D, 2D and keyboard tasks. Design implications (my inference): keep the primary button in the same place across steps so travel distance is near zero, and keep targets well above the finger's precision limit.

findings.claim: Hidden navigation is used less and later than visible navigation, so NN/g recommends visible navigation when there are 4–5 top-level items.
findings.evidence: NN/g (Pernice & Budiu, 2016; 179 users): on mobile, 89% of tasks used navigation on the site with combined visible and hidden navigation, against 44–56% on sites with hidden menus. Navigation was used later when hidden. NN/g's 2015 primer says tab bars become hard to fit beyond five items.

findings.claim: Apple's guidelines say tab bars are for navigation, not actions. They advise against overflow ("More") tabs and against hiding tabs, and ask for single-word labels. On iOS 26 and later the tab bar floats on Liquid Glass and can have a bottom accessory and a separate search tab.
findings.evidence: The HIG tab bars page, updated 8 June 2026, says: "Use a tab bar to support navigation, not to provide actions." It warns that a More tab makes content harder to reach and notice, and keeps the tab bar visible except when a modal covers it.

findings.claim: Apple's guidelines set a 44×44 pt minimum hit area, prefer full-width primary buttons, and say a destructive action should never be the primary button. They also ask for on-screen alternatives to gestures and text enlargement of at least 200%.
findings.evidence: From the HIG Buttons, Accessibility and Typography pages: about 12 pt padding around bezeled controls and 24 pt around unbezeled ones. Dynamic Type Body text goes from 17 pt at the default size up to 53 pt at the largest accessibility size (AX5).

findings.claim: Sheets: use medium and large heights with a grab handle and swipe-to-dismiss, show only one sheet at a time, and use full-screen modals for camera views and multi-step tasks. NN/g adds that sheets need a visible Close button and must close on Back, and that swipe-down should not be the only way out.
findings.evidence: HIG Sheets, updated 24 March 2026, also puts Cancel on the leading edge and Done on the trailing edge of the top bar. NN/g (Laubheimer, 2023) also warns against stacked sheets and against using sheets for long content.

findings.claim: Material 3 allows 3–5 navigation bar destinations. Its 2025 Expressive update lowers the bar from 80 dp to 64 dp. A FAB represents a screen's primary action, and Android recommends touch targets of at least 48×48 dp.
findings.evidence: Sources: the Material Components for Android docs (BottomNavigation.md, FloatingActionButton.md) and Android's accessibility guide.

findings.claim: System edge gestures limit in-app gestures. iOS 26 adds a back gesture that works anywhere in the content area, not just from the edge. Android's back gesture works from both side edges, and apps cannot opt out of its home gesture at the bottom edge.
findings.evidence: Apple's UIKit docs: interactiveContentPopGestureRecognizer (iOS 26.0+) starts a back navigation on a leading-to-trailing pan anywhere in the content area. Android docs: apps can opt out of back only for specific areas via setSystemGestureExclusionRects, cannot opt out of the home gesture, and should pad swipeable views by the system gesture insets. Edge-to-edge is enforced when targeting SDK 35. The cap of about 200 dp per edge comes from secondary sources only.

findings.claim: In Expo SDK 57, native tabs come from expo-router/unstable-native-tabs. They allow at most 5 tabs on Android, cannot report the tab bar height, and support a minimise behaviour, a bottom accessory (iOS 26+) and per-tab icon colours.
findings.evidence: From the Expo docs (v57 reference and native tabs guide). They also say SDK 58 moves the import to expo-router/native-tabs, and that FlatList has limitations with native tabs.

findings.claim: iOS Reachability is off by default (Settings > Accessibility > Touch). When on, a swipe down on the bottom edge lowers the top half of the screen. Samsung One UI's layout puts content you look at in the top "viewing area" and keeps touch controls in the "interaction area" below.
findings.evidence: From Apple's iPhone User Guide (iOS 27 edition, which lists iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max) and Samsung's One UI developer layout guide. SamMobile describes Samsung's separate one-handed mode.

findings.claim: Reference screen sizes in points: iPhone 15/16 393×852, 15/16 Plus 430×932, 17 and 17 Pro 402×874, Air 420×912, 17 Pro Max 440×956, all at @3x and 460 ppi. So 1 pt is about 0.166 mm and 5 tabs on a 393 pt screen are about 13 mm wide each, against about 11.7 mm on the iPhone 7 Hoober studied.
findings.evidence: From compiled device tables (Use Your Loaf). The physical sizes are my own calculations from pixel counts and ppi. Apple's layout page (updated 9 September 2026) no longer shows the size table in its machine-readable version.

spec:
# Vaultwise mobile: thumb-reach model, navigation decision and placement spec

v1, 2026-10-10. Target: Expo SDK 57 (React Native 0.86) on iOS 26/27 and Android 15/16.

Labels used in this spec:
- **[D]** a documented fact from a cited source.
- **[I]** my inference or synthesis.

---

## 0. What the evidence says, in seven lines

1. **Grip varies** [D]
   - About half of people touching the screen use one hand (49%). The rest cradle the phone (36%) or use two hands (15%).
   - One-handed users are 67% right thumb, 33% left (Hoober 2013, 780 people touching the screen).
   - Grips shift constantly, and Hoober withdrew his 2013 reach drawings.
2. **The centre wins** [D]
   - People prefer to touch the centre and are most accurate there: about 7 mm at the centre against about 12 mm at the corners.
   - The top and bottom edges are worse than the sides (Hoober 2013 and 2017).
3. **The comfortable thumb area does not grow with the phone** [D]: about 36 cm² on 4–6 inch phones, and the grip moves up on bigger phones (Le et al., CHI 2018).
   - [I] That is about 39% of a 6.1 inch screen and about 33% of a 6.7 inch screen.
4. **The corner nearest the thumb base is the worst place to tap** [D]: excessive thumb bending there makes it slow and inaccurate (Trudeau et al. 2012).
5. **Targets** [D]
   - Size: 9.2 mm for single taps, 9.6 mm for repeated tapping (Parhi et al. 2006); NN/g says 1 cm.
   - Platform minimums: Apple 44 pt (about 7.3 mm on current iPhones), Android 48 dp, WCAG 2.5.8 24 CSS px.
6. **Navigation** [D]
   - Visible navigation beats hidden (NN/g).
   - Tab bars hold 5 items at most and are for navigation, not actions (Apple HIG, Material, Expo native tabs).
7. **Edges belong to the system** [D]
   - iOS: back swipe from the edge, plus (iOS 26+) a back swipe anywhere in the content area.
   - Android: back swipe from both side edges; the home gesture at the bottom edge cannot be overridden.
   - iOS Reachability uses a swipe down on the bottom edge.

There is no peer-reviewed thumb-reach study on 6.1–6.9 inch phones in the sources I found. The zone model below extrapolates from 4–6 inch data, so it must be checked with the reach test in §8. [I]

---

## 1. Units and reference canvases

| Canvas | Points | Physical size (mm) | Safe area top / bottom | Use it for |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **S** | 393 × 852 | 65.1 × 141.1 | 59 / 34 | iPhone 15/16; also 402 × 874 (iPhone 17/17 Pro; top inset 62) |
| **L** | 430 × 932 | 71.2 × 154.4 | 59 / 34 | 15/16 Plus; also 420 × 912 (Air) and 440 × 956 (17/18 Pro Max) |

**Point-to-millimetre conversion** [I, calculated from 460 ppi @3x]
- 1 pt ≈ 0.166 mm, so 1 mm ≈ 6.0 pt.
- 44 pt ≈ 7.3 mm; 56 pt ≈ 9.3 mm; 64 pt ≈ 10.6 mm; 72 pt ≈ 11.9 mm.
- On Android, design in dp using the same percentage bands.
- Hoober-derived tables that say "31 pt" for 11 mm use typographic points. On iPhone, 11 mm ≈ 66 pt. [I]

---

## 2. Heat-map model: one-handed use, portrait

### 2.1 How the model was built [I]

- **Thumb pivot**
  - Placed about 5 mm outside the holding edge.
  - Vertical position: about 80% of screen height on S, about 75% on L. On larger phones the grip moves up (Le et al.).
- **Distance bands from the pivot**
  - Under 25 mm: **F**, flexion. Reachable, but slow and inaccurate (Trudeau 2012).
  - 25–60 mm: **N**, natural.
  - 60–70 mm: **S**, stretch.
  - Over 70 mm: **H**, hard. Needs a grip shift or the other hand.
- **Why these numbers**
  - The 25–60 mm band reproduces Le et al.'s roughly 36 cm² comfortable area as a sector of about 100–120°.
  - The arc shape follows Bergstrom-Lehtovirta & Oulasvirta's quadratic model.
- **Accuracy layer** (Hoober)
  - Centre: about 7 mm.
  - Top and bottom bands: 11–12 mm.
  - Corners: about 12 mm.
- **Other cells**
  - **X**: system area, no app targets.
  - **B**: bottom band. Reach is natural there, but accuracy is low.
- **Limit of the model:** small hands, roughly the 5th percentile, have markedly less reach. Treat N as the best case and design primary actions for the both-hands sweet spot (§2.4).

### 2.2 Right hand, S (393 × 852)

Columns are 20% of width (about 79 pt each); c1 is the far side from the thumb.

| y% (pt) | c1 | c2 | c3 | c4 | c5 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0–7 (0–59) | X | X | X | X | X |
| 7–30 (59–256) | H | H | H | H | H |
| 30–42 (256–358) | H | H | H | S | S |
| 42–52 (358–443) | H | H | S | N | N |
| 52–62 (443–528) | H | S | N | N | N |
| 62–90 (528–767) | S | N | N | N | F |
| 90–96 (767–818) | S | B | B | B | F |
| 96–100 (818–852), home indicator | X | X | X | X | X |

### 2.3 Right hand, L (430 × 932)

Columns are about 86 pt each.

| y% (pt) | c1 | c2 | c3 | c4 | c5 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0–6 (0–59) | X | X | X | X | X |
| 6–40 (59–373) | H | H | H | H | H |
| 40–50 (373–466) | H | H | H | S | S |
| 50–60 (466–559) | H | H | S | N | N |
| 60–70 (559–652) | H | S | N | N | N |
| 70–90 (652–839) | S | N | N | N | F |
| 90–96 (839–898) | S/H | B | B | B | F |
| 96–100 (898–932) | X | X | X | X | X |

**Left hand:** mirror the columns (c1↔c5, c2↔c4). The vertical bands do not change.

### 2.4 Both-hands sweet spot (the target zone for primary actions)

This is the part of the screen that is natural for both the right and the left thumb.
- **S:** x 20–80% (79–314 pt) by y 62–90% (528–767 pt). The centre column (x 40–60%) is also natural from y 52% (443 pt).
- **L:** x 20–80% (86–344 pt) by y 70–90% (652–839 pt). The centre column is also natural from y 60% (559 pt).
- Anything that must work for every user, one-handed, should have its centre inside this zone or be a full-width bar crossing it.

### 2.5 Corners

| Corner | Right-hand rating | Left-hand rating | Allowed uses |
|---|---|---|---|
| Top-far | Hardest | Hardest | Back or Close (these always have gesture alternatives), avatar, tertiary items |
| Top-near | Hard | Hard | Overflow menu ("…"), Help |
| Bottom-near | Flexion: slow and less accurate | Mirrors to far side | Large, low-frequency targets only, such as tab 5 or the keypad delete key |
| Bottom-far | Stretch on S, near-hard on L | Mirrors to near side | Large targets only |

### 2.6 Minimum size and spacing by region [I, from Hoober, Parhi and HIG]

| Region | Minimum hit area | Minimum centre-to-centre spacing |
|---|---|---|
| Centre (x 15–85%, y 20–80%) | 44 × 44 pt | 48 pt (about 8 mm, above Hoober's 7 mm) |
| Top 20%, bottom 20%, outer 15% columns | 56 pt (≈ 9.3 mm, Parhi's 9.2 mm) | 64–72 pt (10.6–12 mm) |
| Corners | 72 pt effective (visual size + hitSlop) | 72 pt |
| Keypads (repeated tapping) | 64 pt tall (≈ 10.6 mm, at least Parhi's 9.6 mm) | 8 pt gaps |

---

## 3. Navigation architecture (decision)

### 3.1 Recommended: Option A

**Tab order (left to right):** Home · Vaults · **Pay** · Invest · Emergency

**Where each tab falls on S** (tab centres at x = 39, 118, 197, 275, 354 pt; about 13 mm wide each [I]):

| Tab | Right hand | Left hand | Why it sits here |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 Home | Stretch | Flexion | Launch tab, so tapped less often than visited; Home-first is a strong convention |
| 2 Vaults | Natural | Natural | Frequent |
| 3 Pay | Natural | Natural | The only bottom slot natural for both thumbs; time-critical at a till |
| 4 Invest | Natural | Natural | Frequent for Gen Z users [I] |
| 5 Emergency | Flexion | Stretch | Rare but must stay visible; tapping it only opens a screen, so a mis-tap does no harm |

**What happens to the current More tab**
- Settings go behind a **"Profile & settings" avatar**: 44 pt hit area, top-leading in the header of every tab root. This follows Hoober's advice to put tertiary functions in a corner menu.
- The other More items move:
  - Rules and round-ups, and joint vaults → **Vaults**.
  - Receipts and statements → **Vault detail**, plus a **Home "To-do"** card.
  - Assistant → **Home quick action**, plus contextual "Ask why" links.
  - Help and legal → **Profile & settings**.
  - Delete account → **Profile & settings › Account**.

**Why not six tabs** [D]
- Expo native tabs allow at most 5 on Android.
- Material allows 3–5, and NN/g says fitting more than 5 is hard.
- The HIG warns against overflow More tabs.

**Option B (fallback if you want to keep More):** Home · Vaults · Pay · Invest · More. Emergency then leaves the tab bar and appears in four places:
- A pinned "Emergency access" row at the top of Vaults.
- A Home card.
- An app-icon quick action or app shortcut.
- An action on the Health vault.

The cost: one more tap, and the safety promise is visible less often. [I]

### 3.2 Pay is a centre tab, not a raised centre button

- **The HIG says tabs are for navigation, not actions** [D]. Pay is designed as a destination: a scanner-first screen with pending checkouts and code entry.
- **A raised button cannot be built with native tabs** [D]. A protruding custom button needs a JavaScript tab bar (Expo's custom tabs). That loses the native features below. [I, partly D]
  - Liquid Glass and minimise behaviour on iOS.
  - Material behaviour on Android.
  - Automatic right-to-left mirroring (the HIG prefers system components for this).
  - Built-in VoiceOver and TalkBack semantics.
- **A raised button overlaps scrolling content** at the bottom edge, where accuracy is worst (12 mm), and adds a target next to the tab bar. [I, from Hoober]
- **Prominence is still achievable inside a native tab** [D, the Expo docs allow per-tab icon and label colour]:
  - An accent-coloured scan glyph: SF Symbol `qrcode.viewfinder`, Material Symbol `qr_code_scanner`.
  - The single-word label "Pay".
- **Open risk:** users in QR-heavy markets (India, Singapore) may expect a raised Scan button. Test it (§10).

### 3.3 Tab bar implementation (Expo SDK 57)

```tsx
// app/(tabs)/_layout.tsx
import { NativeTabs } from 'expo-router/unstable-native-tabs'; // SDK 58+: 'expo-router/native-tabs'
export default function Tabs() {
  return (
    <NativeTabs minimizeBehavior="never">{/* Pay and Emergency must never collapse away */}
      <NativeTabs.Trigger name="home">{/* Label "Home"; Icon sf house.fill, md home */}</NativeTabs.Trigger>
      <NativeTabs.Trigger name="vaults">{/* "Vaults" */}</NativeTabs.Trigger>
      <NativeTabs.Trigger name="pay">{/* "Pay"; sf qrcode.viewfinder; accent icon colour for this tab */}</NativeTabs.Trigger>
      <NativeTabs.Trigger name="invest">{/* "Invest" */}</NativeTabs.Trigger>
      <NativeTabs.Trigger name="emergency">{/* "Emergency"; neutral colour, not red */}</NativeTabs.Trigger>
    </NativeTabs>
  );
}
```

- **Tabs are fixed.** Never add, remove or disable a tab at runtime; Expo does not support it and the HIG advises against it [D].
- **Badges:** only on Home, and only for action-required items (receipts owed after an emergency withdrawal, or a review that needs the user's input). The HIG reserves badges for critical information.
- **Tab bar height cannot be measured** with native tabs [D]. On tab-root and pushed screens, use `ScrollView contentInsetAdjustmentBehavior="automatic"`. Never pin absolutely positioned controls above the tab bar.
- **Optional (iOS 26+): `NativeTabs.BottomAccessory`** [D, SDK 55+] as a "Pending checkout · Acme · $42 · Resume" mini-bar while a merchant checkout is open. On Android, show the same thing as an inline card at the top of Pay. [I]

---

## 4. Global placement rules

### Primary actions

- **R1 Primary CTA (in modal flows)**
  - Full width minus 16 pt margins on each side (20 pt when the screen is at least 420 pt wide), 56 pt tall.
  - `bottom = safeAreaInsets.bottom + 16` (Android: navigation-bar inset + 16 dp).
  - hitSlop 8 pt above and below, giving an effective height of 72 pt ≈ 12 mm (Hoober's bottom-edge accuracy).
  - Resulting position: S y 746–802 (87.6–94.1%); L y 826–882 (88.6–94.6%).
- **R2 Secondary action**
  - 48 pt tall, tonal or text style, placed **above** the primary with a 12 pt gap. The primary stays closest to the thumb.
  - Two equal-priority actions side by side get equal widths and the same height (HIG).
- **R3 Same slot through a flow** [I, from FFitts]
  - Continue → Confirm → Done always occupy the R1 slot, so travel distance is close to zero.
  - Ignore taps on a newly shown step's CTA for the first **400 ms**, so a double tap cannot carry over into the next step.
  - Irreversible steps change the label and require Face ID or the PIN.
- **R4 No primary CTA pinned above the tab bar.**
  - Tab-root and pushed screens place primary actions **inline** in the sweet spot at scroll-top: S y ≈ 0.52–0.80H, L y ≈ 0.60–0.82H.
  - Every flow that moves money is a full-screen modal that covers the tab bar (HIG modal exception), so R1 applies.

### Destructive actions

- **R5** Destructive actions are never the primary (HIG).
  - They are never within 24 pt of a primary CTA, and never in the R1 slot of a step that usually holds "Continue".
  - They live in the top-trailing "…" menu or at the end of a settings group.
  - They are always followed by a confirmation where the safe option is the default. Money actions also need biometrics or the PIN.
  - Never rely on a hard-to-reach position for safety: users shift their grip (Hoober). [D + I]

### Header actions

- **R6**
  - At most 1 leading item (Back, Close or avatar) and 2 trailing items (overflow, Help or "+"). Hit area 44 × 44 pt; glyph 22–24 pt.
  - Header items are for navigation and tertiary actions only.
  - Any frequent action in the header needs an in-content twin in the sweet spot.
  - Back is also reachable by swipe on both platforms, so the top-leading Back button is acceptable.

### Sheets or full screens

**R7**

| Use | Presentation |
|---|---|
| Choosing 1 of up to 8 options (vault picker, reason, filter) | Sheet at medium height (about half the screen), with grab handle **and** a visible Close button. Options are listed from the top, so at medium height they land in the lower half by construction. [I] |
| Explanations, receipt detail, "Why was this declined?" | Sheet, medium then expandable to large |
| Withdraw, Emergency request, Pay checkout, transfers | `fullScreenModal`. Close (X) top-leading; Back steps back one step. |
| Camera and document review | `fullScreenModal` (HIG) |
| PIN entry | `fullScreenModal`, or a step inside the flow's modal |
| Vault, transaction and holding detail; Settings | Push within the tab's stack |
| Assistant chat | `fullScreenModal` (long content, so not a sheet, per NN/g) |

- Never stack sheets. Close one before opening the next (HIG and NN/g).
- Android Back must close any sheet or modal (NN/g; predictive back).

### Keypads

- **R8 Amount keypad**
  - 3 columns by 4 rows; keys 64 pt tall (68 pt when the screen is at least 900 pt tall) by (W − 32)/3 wide; 8 pt gaps; total height 280–296 pt.
  - Bottom edge = CTA top − 16 pt.
  - Position: S y 450–730 (52.8–85.7%); L y 530–810 (56.9–86.9%). Entirely inside the sweet spot plus its centre column.
  - Bottom row: decimal separator (locale-specific) · 0 · delete (⌫ at bottom-trailing, the platform convention).
- **R9 PIN pad**
  - Same key size. No CTA: it submits automatically on the last digit.
  - Bottom edge = `insets.bottom + 48`.
  - Position: S y 490–770 (57.5–90.4%); L y 554–850 (59.4–91.2%).
  - Bottom row: [Face ID / fingerprint] · 0 · ⌫. Never shuffle the key layout.

### List rows and swipe gestures

- **R10 Rows**
  - At least 56 pt tall (Hoober: 9–10 mm for rows that reach the screen edge). The whole row or card is tappable.
  - Cards have 16 pt side margins, so swipes start outside the system's back-gesture zone.
- **R11 Swipe actions**
  - **Trailing swipe only** (right to left in left-to-right languages): non-destructive actions such as "Add money" or "Pin to Home".
  - No full-swipe execution, and no leading swipe actions anywhere.
  - Every swipe action is repeated in a long-press menu and on the detail screen (HIG: offer alternatives to gestures).

### Edges and system gestures

- **R12**
  - (a) On pushed screens, no custom left-to-right horizontal pan, carousel paging or chart scrubbing. iOS 26's content-area back gesture would steal it [D]. Horizontal carousels are allowed only on tab roots.
  - (b) Charts scrub on press-and-hold, then drag, with 24 pt side insets.
  - (c) No custom gesture may start at the bottom edge (iOS home and Reachability; the Android home gesture cannot be overridden [D]).
  - (d) Use `setSystemGestureExclusionRects` only for an edge-touching slider, and keep it under 200 dp per edge.
  - (e) Opt in to Android predictive back.

### Scrolling

- **R13** Tab-root and list screens get **96 pt of extra bottom padding** beyond the automatic inset, so the last item can be scrolled into the middle of the screen (Hoober).

### Size and spacing

- **R14** Apply the minimum hit areas and spacing in §2.6.
- Padding around elements: 12 pt around bezeled controls, 24 pt around unbezeled ones (HIG).

## 5. Screen-by-screen rules

Positions are given as S / L fractions of screen height (H), measured at scroll-top.

1. **Home (tab root)**
   - **Header row:** avatar top-leading (Profile & settings); notifications bell top-trailing.
   - **Viewing area (non-interactive), 0.08–0.38H / 0.08–0.45H:** total balance, "safe to spend", and lock status. Large, centred, nothing to tap. This follows One UI's split of a top viewing area and a lower interaction area.
   - **Quick-actions row, 0.45–0.55H / 0.50–0.60H:** 4 equal tiles, each 72 pt tall with a 64 pt icon area and a label: Add money · Withdraw · Upload receipt · Ask.
   - **"To-do" cards** (receipts owed, review needs input) come next, then the vaults carousel (horizontal is allowed on a root screen; 16 pt inset), then recent activity.
   - **Large text:** at accessibility sizes, collapse the hero to one line so the quick actions stay in the 0.5–0.9H band.
2. **Vaults list (tab root)**
   - **Top of screen:** large title. Top-trailing "+" (New vault). Pinned row "Rules & round-ups" above the list.
   - **Vault cards:** 88 pt tall (name, balance, goal bar, lock/joint badges), grouped into "My vaults" and "Joint".
   - **End of list:** a full-width dashed "+ New vault" card, the in-content twin of the header "+".
   - **Gestures:** trailing swipe gives "Add money". Long-press menu: Add money / Pin to Home / Rules.
3. **Vault detail (pushed; tab bar stays visible)**
   - **Header:** Back top-leading. "…" top-trailing for Rename, Rules, Members, Statements, Close vault (destructive, opens a dedicated confirmation screen per R5).
   - **Hero, 0.08–0.48H / 0.08–0.55H:** balance, goal ring, purpose.
   - **Inline action row directly below the hero, at 0.50–0.58H / 0.57–0.65H:** two 56 pt buttons of equal width, "Add money" (tonal) and "Withdraw" (filled).
   - **Below:** activity list with receipts.
   - **No** sticky bar (the tab bar height cannot be measured).
4. **Withdraw amount (`fullScreenModal`)**
   - **Header:** Close top-leading; title "Withdraw · Health" centred.
   - **Amount, 0.12–0.28H:** 56 pt bold numerals, auto-shrinking. Below it, "Available $X · Limit $Y".
   - **Vault/purpose chip, 0.32–0.38H:** stretch zone, changed rarely; opens a medium sheet.
   - **Keypad:** per R8.
   - **CTA:** "Continue" per R1, disabled until the amount is valid.
   - **Next steps:** proof capture (5), then verification (6), then PIN (8).
5. **Camera capture (`fullScreenModal`)**
   - **Viewfinder:** full-bleed, with a document guide frame centred at 0.14–0.62H and a hint at 0.66H.
   - **Page thumbnails strip:** 0.72–0.78H.
   - **Control row, centred on `H − insets.bottom − 80`** (S y 738, L y 818):
     - Shutter: 72 pt circle, centred.
     - "Photos" (system picker): 56 pt, leading.
     - Flash: 56 pt, trailing.
   - **Header:** Close top-leading; Tips top-trailing.
   - **Review state, same modal:** "Use photo" as the R1 CTA; "Retake" as the R2 secondary.
   - Android Back returns to capture.
6. **Verifying (a state within the flow modal)**
   - **Centre:** progress animation at 0.30–0.55H. Step list ("Reading invoice · Checking merchant · Matching purpose") at 0.55–0.72H.
   - **While processing:** only "Continue in background" (tonal, in the R1 slot).
   - **Results, primary in the R1 slot:**
     - Approved: "Done".
     - Declined: "See why" (opens the Assistant explanation sheet), with secondary "Try another document".
     - Needs human review: "Done", with secondary "Add a note for reviewer".
   - Back or Close during processing means "continue in background", **not** cancel.
7. **Emergency request**
   - **Tab root:**
     - Hero, 0.08–0.35H: what is available now (Tier 1 amount) and plain guardrails.
     - Two tier cards, each at least 96 pt, at 0.38–0.68H / 0.42–0.72H.
     - Inline primary "Get emergency money" (56 pt, full width) at 0.72–0.79H / 0.74–0.80H, with at least 24 pt of clearance above the tab bar.
     - A "Receipts owed" card sits at the top of the content when relevant.
   - **Flow (`fullScreenModal`):**
     - Amount: R8.
     - Reason: 2-column chip grid, 56 pt chips, at 0.40–0.80H.
     - Review: summary plus hold time; CTA "Confirm with Face ID".
     - PIN (Tier 2).
     - Hold countdown: centred at 0.35–0.55H. "Cancel request" is a 48 pt secondary at about 0.65H, **not** in the R1 slot. "Done" is in the R1 slot.
   - No camera step up front (receipts come afterwards).
8. **PIN confirm (`fullScreenModal` or flow step)**
   - **What is being authorised, 0.10–0.32H:** amount, source vault, destination merchant or account.
   - **PIN dots:** centred at 0.40H. Errors at 0.45H. "Forgot PIN?" text button at 0.48H.
   - **Keypad:** per R9.
   - Face ID is attempted automatically first. Close (top-leading) cancels the authorisation. No swipe-to-dismiss.
9. **Invest (tab root)**
   - **Top:** large title, then a segmented control "Core | Practice", tap only (tabs at the top for switching views, per Hoober).
   - **Hero, 0.18–0.45H:** value and chart (press-and-hold scrub, per R12).
   - **Inline action row, 0.50–0.58H / 0.55–0.63H:** "Change monthly plan" (filled) and "Add lump sum" (tonal).
   - **Below:** holdings list.
   - **Practice mode:**
     - A persistent "Practice — virtual money" banner in the hero.
     - Instrument detail is pushed.
     - The trade ticket is a sheet expandable from medium to large, with "Place practice order" in the R1 position inside the sheet.
10. **Profile & settings** (replaces More; opened from the avatar; pushed)
    - Grouped rows, 56 pt tall, ordered by frequency: Security (Face ID, PIN, devices) → Limits & emergency settings → Notifications → Country & currency → Help & legal → Account.
    - **Sign out** and **Delete account** are the last rows, in red text.
    - **Delete account** opens a dedicated screen:
      - Consequences, including that vault balances must be withdrawn first.
      - An acknowledgement checkbox.
      - The R1 slot shows "Delete account…" in destructive *outline* style, enabled only after the checkbox is ticked.
      - Then a system alert (Cancel is the default) and Face ID or PIN.
11. **Pay checkout (`fullScreenModal`)**
    - **Entry points:** a scan on the Pay tab, a universal link or app link from the merchant, or a notification.
    - **Header:** Close top-leading.
    - **Merchant block, 0.08–0.22H:** logo, name, verified-merchant badge.
    - **Amount, 0.22–0.32H.**
    - **"View invoice" row, 0.33–0.40H** (occasional use).
    - **"Pay from" vault card, 0.44–0.56H / 0.48–0.60H:** shows why it matched (for example "Health — pharmacy invoice"). "Change" opens a medium sheet; ineligible vaults are shown disabled with the reason.
    - **Verification status row, 0.58–0.66H:** Checking, then Verified.
    - **CTA "Pay $42.00"** in the R1 slot: disabled until verified, then Face ID, with a PIN step as fallback.
    - **Success:** "Done" in the same slot.
    - **Pay tab root (scanner-first):**
      - The viewfinder runs **only while the tab is focused**, in 0–0.62H, with the aiming frame at about 0.30H. Aiming moves the phone, not the thumb.
      - Panel at 0.62–0.90H: a "Pending checkouts" card, then "Enter merchant code" and "Torch", both 56 pt.
      - Without camera permission, show the settled camera primer inline.
12. **Assistant chat (`fullScreenModal`)**
    - **Header:** Close top-leading; "New chat" top-trailing.
    - **Messages:** newest at the bottom.
    - **Suggested-prompt chips:** directly above the composer, horizontal row allowed (root-level modal, 16 pt inset).
    - **Composer:** full width, at least 48 pt tall, grows to 5 lines, with Send (44 pt) trailing. It sits on top of the keyboard.
    - **Action cards from the assistant** (for example "Move $20 to Health") put their button at the bottom of the card. Tapping it opens the standard money flow with PIN; nothing executes directly from chat.

## 6. Left-handed use

- **No handedness setting** [I]. Hoober found users switch hands and grips constantly and cannot predict their own grip. Make primary placements **symmetric** instead:
  - Full-width CTAs.
  - Centred shutter, PIN pad and Pay tab.
  - Equal-width button pairs.
  - No FAB pinned to one corner.
- **Zones mirror for left-handed users** (§2). On the tab bar, Home becomes the flexion corner and Emergency becomes the far stretch. Both are acceptable for their frequency.
- **Keep platform conventions** even where they slightly favour the right hand (the ⌫ key at bottom-trailing, Back at top-leading). Convention outweighs a small ergonomic gain. [I]
- **Right-to-left languages (Arabic in the UAE):**
  - Use start/end, never left/right.
  - Native tabs and stacks mirror automatically (HIG layout guidance).
  - Test which edge the iOS back gesture uses in right-to-left on a device.

## 7. Accessibility

- **Dynamic Type up to AX5** (Body text 17 to 53 pt; the HIG asks for at least 200%):
  - CTAs keep a 56 pt *minimum* height but may grow, with labels of up to 2 lines.
  - At AX1 and above, side-by-side buttons become a vertical stack with the primary at the bottom.
  - Collapse heroes so actions stay in the 0.5–0.9H band.
  - Keypad digits scale up to 1.5×; keys never go below 64 pt.
  - The large amount display uses `adjustsFontSizeToFit` and an accessibility label with the full amount.
  - Leave tab labels to the native implementation.
- **Reachability** is off by default [D], so never rely on it. Make sure no app gesture starts at the bottom edge, so the iOS Reachability gesture and Samsung's one-handed mode keep working.
- **Gestures:** every gesture has a tap alternative. Label every control for VoiceOver, TalkBack and Voice Control.
- **Targets:** meet 44 pt (iOS) and 48 dp (Android) everywhere, and the larger region minimums in §2.6. WCAG 2.5.8 (24 CSS px) is then met automatically.
- **Test matrix:** S and L canvases at text sizes Large (default), xxxL, AX3 and AX5. Also test a right-to-left locale and one-handed use with each hand.

## 8. Checking the model: an in-app reach test

1. Build a dev-only route, `/dev/reach-test`: a 5 × 10 grid of 44 pt targets at the cell centres, lit in random order.
2. Participants:
   - At least 12 people (at least 4 left-handed), with hand lengths spread like Le et al.'s 163–219 mm.
   - Each uses one 6.1–6.3 inch phone and one 6.7–6.9 inch phone.
   - Standing, one-handed; one round with the dominant hand and one with the non-dominant hand.
3. Log the tap coordinates, the offset from the target centre, the time from prompt to tap, and hit or miss.
4. Per cell, compute the median time and the 95% error radius, then recolour §2.
5. **Rule:** move any primary action whose cell has an error radius larger than half the target size, or a time more than 1.5× the centre median.

## 9. Expo SDK 57 notes

- **Tabs:** `expo-router/unstable-native-tabs` (`NativeTabs`). 5-tab cap on Android. Tab bar height is not measurable. FlatList limits apply (use `disableTransparentOnScrollEdge` if the bar renders transparent). `minimizeBehavior` options: never / onScrollDown. `BottomAccessory` needs SDK 55+.
- **Modals:** `presentation: 'fullScreenModal'` for flows. For sheets, use `formSheet` with detents and a grabber. Check the react-native-screens prop names against the SDK 57 docs.
- **Safe areas and back:** use `react-native-safe-area-context` `useSafeAreaInsets()` for R1 and R9. On Android, use `BackHandler` and predictive back as in R7 and in screen 6 (Verifying).
- **Device check:** whether `gestureEnabled:false` also disables iOS 26's `interactiveContentPopGestureRecognizer` in react-native-screens is unverified. Test it on a device.
